description:
Issue summary:
Edge CDN (conditional GET / If-None-Match probe) is intermittently issuing a 304-ish probe/teardown while an SSE stream to a long-running generation is active. The downstream behavior observed by the customer: the stream abruptly ends mid-markdown block (no explicit terminal event), and on immediate reconnect the new stream begins with a repeated system/preamble message and a duplicated short token prefix. This results in partial content, duplicated system content, and a broken markdown code block for some sessions.

Impact:
- PaperTrail Analytics (enterprise) reports ~12% of long-form streaming calls truncated or duplicated over last 24h from us-east.
- Affected flows are interactive summarization and long-code-generation where the client depends on a consistent stream boundary and finalization marker.
- Customer sees degraded UX (broken markdown/code fences) and increased downstream parsing errors.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east edge region fronted by third-party CDN (conditional caching + revalidation enabled).
- Requests are to /v1/stream?model=redwood/ranger-7b with SSE.

Observed timing:
- Typical timeline: initial SSE open -> ~30–90s of streamed tokens -> CDN issues conditional revalidate (If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since) -> TCP/HTTP teardown from CDN side -> client reconnects and resumes -> duplicated "system" preamble and missing closing fence.

Notes: Customer is on enterprise plan with dedicated routing rules. They provided sample client logs and a session id (session_id: pt-9a7f).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a client to open SSE to /v1/stream?model=redwood/ranger-7b with Accept: text/event-stream and keep the connection open for >60s.
2) Put a caching CDN in front (simulate conditional revalidation on TTL expiry). Set CDN to send conditional GETs (If-None-Match) periodically for long-lived connections.
3) Trigger a long generation (300–800 tokens). Observe stream through client until CDN issues conditional probe.

4) When CDN sends revalidation (or the edge issues a FIN), observe whether origin emits terminal marker (data: [DONE]) or connection closes silently, then reconnect the client and inspect the leading tokens on the resumed stream.
5) Repeat with smaller and larger keepalive/heartbeat intervals to reproduce frequency variance.
observed_behavior: Partial output: stream ends without explicit terminal event; client reconnect receives a fresh initial 'system' message repeated, followed by a short duplicated token prefix. Final markdown code block frequently lacks closing backticks, causing downstream parser failure.
expected_behavior: If the origin marks the stream finished the SSE should include an explicit terminal event (e.g., data: [DONE]) before close. If CDN revalidation occurs mid-stream, edge should hold or proxy the request such that clients either receive the terminal marker or can resume without duplicating system-level messages.
logs: [2026-03-13T11:22:41.123Z] SSE open session pt-9a7f: received token 'defense'...
[2026-03-13T11:23:12.002Z] tcp RST from CDN-edge (conditional-get probe) - connection closed without terminal event
[2026-03-13T11:23:12.120Z] client reconnect session pt-9a7f: receives 'system: <preamble>' then 'system: <preamble>' (duplicate), then content starts mid-sentence
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 12:00 - Initial triage by Support (Ava T): reproduces with internal simple CDN config and logs show connection FIN from CDN during revalidation.

2026-03-13 13:30 - SRE (Diego M) observed that origin runtime does not always emit finalization marker when connection is closed by a close-from-proxy; it relies on TCP graceful close to trigger emitter flush.

Hypothesis: Edge/proxy or CDN is issuing conditional GETs that cause a half-close path; origin flush path is skipped leading to silent-close. On reconnect the session handshake includes system preamble generated by the server-side conversation snapshot; session resume logic currently prepends the system preamble unconditionally which creates duplication.
Checked recent deploys: no recent changes to resume/preamble code in last week; CDN config changed yesterday (shorter revalidate TTL) per customer support notes.
Captured pcap between CDN and edge to inspect FIN timing; awaiting redacted pcap from customer for timeline correlation.
mitigation: Applied short-term workaround: disable CDN revalidation for SSE endpoints for PaperTrail's routing rule (edge rule updated at 2026-03-14T02:14Z). Customer implemented a client-side heuristic to wait 200ms for terminal marker before treating the stream as complete. This reduced incidence to ~1.8% in initial sampling.
next_steps: 1) Engineering: add logic in serving-runtime to emit terminal marker immediately on SIGPIPE/connection-abort to avoid silent close. 2) Platform: add edge rule to detect conditional GET on live SSE and hold revalidation until stream finalizes or use cache-bypass for active connections. 3) QA: add integration test simulating conditional revalidation to prevent regressions. 4) Follow up with CDN provider to understand conditional-get behavior on long-lived SSE streams.
resolution: In progress: temporary edge rule applied and customer workaround accepted. Engineering action item created (ENG-STREAM-678) to ensure runtime always flushes finalization marker on abrupt upstream close. Target fix in next minor release.
comments: 2026-03-13 12:05 - Ava Thompson: Reproduced with internal CDN simulator. Attaching minimal repro steps to ticket.
2026-03-13 13:40 - Diego Martinez: Found origin flush path skipped when process sees connection close during streaming. Adding tracepoints to emitter pipeline.
2026-03-13 16:22 - PaperTrail Support (customer): We can confirm behavior reduces when TTL bumped from 30s -> 5m. Happy to accept workaround but want permanent fix.
2026-03-14 02:20 - Platform Ops (Lina Huang): Edge rule to bypass conditional revalidate for /v1/stream updated for PaperTrail routing. Monitoring for 24h.
2026-03-14 09:05 - Diego Martinez: Created ENG ticket ENG-STREAM-678 and linked PR https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/998 to force emit terminal marker on abort. QA scheduled.
2026-03-14 11:00 - Ava Thompson: Customer notified of planned release window next week; keeping ticket open until release and post-release verification.
